# 1. Overview

Extended Data Fig 1 presents host use across Danaini as a butterfly species by
plant genus matrix, aligned to a butterfly phylogeny on one axis and a plant
phylogeny on the other. The butterfly phylogeny is built first, in notebooks 1–3
(Danaini tree generation); the figure itself is assembled in notebooks 4–6:

4. **`4_build_plant_tree.Rmd`** (this notebook) assembles the genus-level
   Apocynaceae and Moraceae phylogeny that orders the matrix columns.
5. `5_build_host_matrix.Rmd` derives the butterfly species by plant genus
   presence/absence matrix from the HOSTS host-record dataset.
6. `6_plot_host_matrix_figure.Rmd` assembles the final figure.

This notebook records the provenance of the plant phylogeny and need only be
re-run when its source trees change; notebooks 5 and 6 read its output,
`input_data/host_matrix/Apo_Mora_phylo_tree/apocynaceae_moraceae_genus_tree.newick`.

The plant phylogeny is assembled from two published sources. The Apocynaceae
backbone is taken from the time-calibrated phylogeny of
[Fishbein et al. (2018)](https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/ecology-and-evolution/articles/10.3389/fevo.2021.719741/full),
reduced to one representative tip per genus, and the Moraceae lineages from a
genus-level chronogram obtained from [TimeTree](https://timetree.org/).
Apocynaceae and Moraceae are not sister families; the two genus-level trees are
therefore joined onto a two-lineage backbone solely to place the families
side by side as the two blocks of host plants used by Danaini. The deep
divergence implied by the backbone is not meaningful and is not interpreted.

```{r setup, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(warning = FALSE, message = FALSE)

library(ape)
library(ggtree)

tree_dir <- "../input_data/host_matrix/Apo_Mora_phylo_tree"
```

# 2. Apocynaceae: reduce the species tree to one tip per genus

The Fishbein et al. (2018) phylogeny samples approximately 1,041 species. Because
the figure resolves host use at the genus level, the tree is reduced to a single
representative tip per genus following the standard phytools procedure
(<https://blog.phytools.org/2014/11/pruning-trees-to-one-member-per-genus.html>):
the genus is parsed from each tip label, the first tip encountered for each genus
is retained, the remaining tips are dropped, and the surviving tips are relabelled
with their genus name.

```{r apocynaceae-genus}
apoc_species <- read.tree(
  file.path(tree_dir, "1041_Fishbein et al. 2018[outgroups_removed].newick")
)

# Genus = text before the first underscore in each "Genus_species" tip label
apoc_genus_of_tip <- sapply(strsplit(apoc_species$tip.label, "_"), `[`, 1)

# First tip encountered for each genus
genera            <- unique(apoc_genus_of_tip)
representative_tip <- sapply(genera, function(g) which(apoc_genus_of_tip == g)[1])

apoc_genus <- drop.tip(
  apoc_species,
  apoc_species$tip.label[-representative_tip]
)
apoc_genus$tip.label <- genera

cat("Apocynaceae genera retained:", length(apoc_genus$tip.label), "\n")
```

# 3. Moraceae: genus-level tree and nomenclature

The Moraceae component is a time-calibrated, genus-level tree of the family
obtained from [TimeTree](https://timetree.org/), which synthesizes published
molecular divergence-time estimates into a consensus chronogram; branch lengths
are expressed in millions of years. Two versions are retained in
`input_data/host_matrix/Apo_Mora_phylo_tree/`: the species-level tree as downloaded
(`moraceae_species.nwk`) and the genus-level tree used here
(`moraceae_genus.nwk`), which spans the ~37 currently recognized Moraceae genera.

The Moraceae genera represented among Danaini host records are *Ficus*,
*Streblus* and *Trophis*. Historical records employ several synonyms, which are
reconciled to currently accepted genera following Plants of the World Online
(POWO, <https://powo.science.kew.org/>): *Cephalotrophis* and *Malaisia* are
treated as *Trophis* (both referring to *Trophis scandens*), and *Urostigma*,
a subgenus of *Ficus*, is treated as *Ficus*. The genus *Trophis* is not
monophyletic in the TimeTree source and is represented by two lineages
(`Trophis-1`, `Trophis-2`); the lineage corresponding to *Trophis scandens*
(`Trophis-1`) is retained and relabelled `Trophis`.

```{r moraceae-genus}
moraceae <- read.tree(file.path(tree_dir, "moraceae_genus.nwk"))

moraceae$tip.label[moraceae$tip.label == "Trophis-1"] <- "Trophis"

cat("Moraceae tips:", paste(sort(moraceae$tip.label), collapse = ", "), "\n")
```

# 4. Join Apocynaceae and Moraceae

The two genus-level trees are bound onto a two-tip backbone and the placeholder
tips removed, yielding a single tree in which all Apocynaceae genera form one
block and all Moraceae genera form another.

```{r graft}
backbone <- read.tree(text = "(Apoc_placeholder:1,Mora_placeholder:1);")

# Graft Apocynaceae
grafted <- bind.tree(
  backbone, apoc_genus,
  where = which(backbone$tip.label == "Apoc_placeholder")
)
grafted <- drop.tip(grafted, "Apoc_placeholder")

# Graft Moraceae (tip indices change after the first drop, so re-find the tip)
grafted <- bind.tree(
  grafted, moraceae,
  where = which(grafted$tip.label == "Mora_placeholder")
)
plant_tree <- drop.tip(grafted, "Mora_placeholder")

cat("Grafted plant tree tips:", length(plant_tree$tip.label), "\n")
```

```{r preview, fig.width=6, fig.height=10}
ggtree(plant_tree, branch.length = "none", ladderize = FALSE) +
  geom_tiplab(size = 1.8, offset = 0.2)
```

# 5. Write the tree

The assembled genus-level tree is written to `input_data/host_matrix/Apo_Mora_phylo_tree/`
for use by the downstream notebooks. (An equivalent tree produced by an earlier
workflow was stored as `apocynacear_moraceae__genus_final_tree.newick`; the
filename used here corrects that spelling. The two describe the same joined
Apocynaceae and Moraceae genus-level tree.)

```{r write}
out_path <- file.path(tree_dir, "apocynaceae_moraceae_genus_tree.newick")
write.tree(plant_tree, out_path)
cat("Wrote:", out_path, "\n")
```
